prev_row.device_notes: This one row is Psalm 70's entire parent grouping. Psalm 70 stands in a typed doublet relation with Psalm 40's closing plea (web:Ps.40.13-Ps.40.17 = oshb:Ps.40.14-Ps.40.18), a free-standing recension of the same composition. Psalm 40 opens ‘רְצֵ֣ה יְ֭הוָה’ (oshb:Ps.40.14), “Be pleased, Yahweh, to deliver me” (web:Ps.40.13); Psalm 70's own opening reads ‘אֱלֹהִ֥ים…’ (oshb:Ps.70.2), “Hurry, God, to deliver me” (web:Ps.70.1), substituting Elohim for the earlier of Psalm 40's two Yahweh tokens. Both psalms share a matching mid-verse clause (words 8-9 of 11 in each host verse, not verse-final): Psalm 40 reads ‘יִגְדַּ֣ל יְהוָ֑ה’ (oshb:Ps.40.17), “Let Yahweh be exalted!” (web:Ps.40.16); Psalm 70's own reads ‘יִגְדַּ֣ל אֱלֹהִ֑ים’ (oshb:Ps.70.5), “Let God be exalted!” (web:Ps.70.4) — a one-word divine-name substitution in an otherwise matching clause. Both psalms' own actual closes come later — Psalm 40 at web:Ps.40.17 (“Don't delay, my God”), Psalm 70 at web:Ps.70.5 (“Yahweh, don't delay”), as this row's own rationale already states for Psalm 70. This Elohim/Yahweh texture is this row's own legitimate discussion, not a boundary driver, since the psalm is chunked whole; it addresses Psalm 70's own text and makes no claim about which composition is prior.
